frequency_question: How often do proposed disruptive trade tariffs or protectionist barriers against allied trade partners proceed to full implementation rather than being watered down, delayed indefinitely, or replaced by a negotiated agreement?
membership_rule: Includes formally announced, highly contested unilateral tariff threats or executive actions targeting close trading partners where commercial stakeholders and bureaucratic friction mobilize to block or modify them. Excludes broad multi-lateral trade rounds or routine anti-dumping duties.

cases.name: US Threat of Tariffs on Mexico over Border Security

provenance_note: claimed 2 hits but 3 of 5 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 5 major prominent instances enumerated; representing a larger class of roughly 12 contested executive trade restriction threats.
known_gaps: Does not fully capture minor or non-publicized administrative trade adjustments.
skeleton: Threatened major protectionist actions categorized by whether integrated supply chain friction and negotiation pressure successfully derailed them prior to execution.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 5 named prominent major bilateral friction cases where severe disruption was threatened.
validity_reason: Structural friction between executive trade policy tools and integrated continental supply chains remains stable across political cycles.
